If it’s positive, you get two real solutions; if zero, one real solution; if negative, complex solutions. Next, plug into the quadratic formula: x = [-b ± √(discriminant)] / (2a). Finally, simplify the result.

replies.Briefly, how do you perform a Principal: PCA reduces data dimensions by finding directions (principal components) that capture the most variance. First, standardize your data. Then, compute the covariance matrix and its eigenvectors/values. The eigenvectors give the new axes, and the eigenvalues show variance explained. Don’t worry—math is just a tool; focus on the goal: simplifying data without losing key patterns.
